QwQ-32B는 Qwen 팀이 강화학습(RL) 확장을 연구해 만든 320: QwQ-32B is a 32-billion-parameter reasoning model built by the Qwen team through research on scaling reinforcement learning (RL), and it states that it delivers performance comparable to DeepSeek-R1, which has 671 billion parameters. It was trained with outcome-based rewards: an accuracy verifier checks math answers, and a code execution server checks whether code is correct. It also includes agent capabilities that use tools and adjust reasoning based on environment feedback. The weights are released under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and ModelScope, and it can also be used through Qwen Chat and the Alibaba Cloud DashScope API.

Code World Model(CWM)은 Meta FAIR CodeGen: Code World Model (CWM) is a 32-billion-parameter dense language model built by the Meta FAIR CodeGen team for research on code generation and code reasoning. To better represent how code and commands change program and system state, it was mid-trained on Python execution traces and agent interaction data from containerized environments. It was then post-trained with multi-task reinforcement learning in verifiable coding, math, and multi-turn software engineering environments. It is released under a non-commercial research license, access requires agreeing to provide contact information, and when quantized it can run on a single 80GB GPU.

ALIGN은 Google Research가 ICML 2021에 발표한 논: ALIGN is the method from the paper 'Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision', presented by Google Research at ICML 2021. Using over 1 billion image–alt-text pairs collected without expensive filtering, a simple dual encoder is trained to align image and text representations with a contrastive loss. The authors state that the scale of the data offsets the noise, achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet and VTAB classification transfer and on Flickr30K and MSCOCO retrieval. The learned representations enable cross-modal retrieval using text and text+image queries.

Flamingo는 DeepMind가 2022년 4월 논문 사전공개본으로: Flamingo is a single visual language model introduced by DeepMind in an April 2022 paper preprint. It takes prompts that mix images, videos, and text as input and outputs answers in language. It states that it achieved top performance in few-shot learning, where a new task can be solved without additional training by putting just a few task-specific examples in the prompt. Across the 16 tasks studied, it outperformed all previous few-shot methods using only 4 examples per task. It combines a separately pretrained, frozen large language model (Chinchilla 70B) with visual representations by inserting new architecture between them, and the final model has 80B parameters.

DETR(DEtection TRansformer)은 객체 탐지를 직접적인: DETR (DEtection TRansformer) is a model that treats object detection as a direct set prediction problem, consisting of a set-based global loss that forces unique predictions via bipartite matching and a transformer encoder-decoder architecture. Using a small set of learned object queries, it reasons about the relations between objects and the global image context to output the final predictions in parallel. It states that with a ResNet-50 backbone it achieves the same COCO 42 AP as Faster R-CNN with half the computation. The repository provides PyTorch training code, pretrained models, a Colab notebook, and a Detectron2 wrapper.

LLaVA(Large Language and Vision Assistan: LLaVA (Large Language and Vision Assistant) is a large multimodal model for general-purpose visual and language understanding. It connects a CLIP ViT-L/14 vision encoder to a Vicuna language model with a simple projection matrix. It was the first attempt at visual instruction tuning, using multimodal instruction-following data generated with language-only GPT-4. It was fine-tuned for two uses, everyday-user visual chat and science QA, and the authors state that combined with GPT-4 it reached the best performance on Science QA at 92.53%. Data, model, and code are released, but licensed for research use only.

Starting with Tesseract 4, an LSTM neural network engine focused on line-level recognition was added, and the legacy engine from Tesseract 3 is still supported. Of its 1,865 tasks across 41 repositories, a public set of 731 is used for the public leaderboard, and to reduce contamination, tasks were taken from repositories under strong copyleft licenses such as GPL. Professional engineers build Docker-based reproducible environments, and humans augment the problem descriptions and requirements. The ranking metric is the Resolve Rate, the percentage of tasks that satisfy both conditions: passing the new tests and keeping existing tests passing.

Sol Video Inference Engine은 추가 학습 없이 비디오: Sol Video Inference Engine is an agent-based framework that accelerates video diffusion model inference without additional training. It combines five techniques, caching, sparse attention, token pruning, quantization, and kernel fusion, into a deployment stack tailored to each model, hardware, and serving setup. Per-technique skill agents test whether each applies, an integration agent bundles the candidates, and human verifiers give feedback on efficiency and quality. It reports end-to-end speedups of more than 2x with almost no loss in visual quality on Cosmos3-Super, LTX-2.3, and SANA-Video.

MLX는 Apple 머신러닝 연구팀이 만든 Apple 실리콘용 머신러닝: MLX is a machine learning array framework for Apple silicon, created by Apple's machine learning research team. It provides a NumPy-like Python API as well as C++, C, and Swift APIs, and higher-level packages such as mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers can be used much like PyTorch. Operations are executed lazily and computation graphs are built dynamically, and because arrays live in shared (unified) memory, computation runs without moving data between the CPU and GPU. On macOS it is installed with pip, and there are also a CUDA backend for Linux and a CPU-only package.

pgvector는 벡터를 다른 데이터와 함께 Postgres에 저장하고: pgvector is an extension that lets you store vectors in Postgres alongside your other data and run exact and approximate nearest neighbor search. It supports single-precision, half-precision, binary, and sparse vectors, along with L2, inner product, cosine, L1, Hamming, and Jaccard distances. It can be used from any language that has a Postgres client, and you get Postgres features such as ACID, point-in-time recovery, and JOINs as they are. When you have many vectors, you can scale with quantization.

Annoy(Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Y: Annoy (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah) is a C++ library that finds points close to a query point, and it provides Python bindings. Because index creation and loading are separate, you can pass an index around as a file and load it into memory quickly. Spotify uses it in music recommendation to search for similar items among user and track vectors.

Apache Iceberg is a high-performance format for huge analytic tables. It brings the reliability and simplicity of SQL tables to big data, letting engines such as Spark, Trino, Flink, Presto, Hive, and Impala safely work with the same tables at the same time. It supports merge, update, and delete SQL, schema evolution without rewriting tables, hidden partitioning, time travel and rollback, and data compaction. The core Java library is the reference implementation.

As long as you have a function that outputs per-class probabilities, it can explain any black-box classifier with two or more classes, and scikit-learn classifiers are supported out of the box. Using algorithms such as Integrated Gradients, TCAV, and TracIn, it shows which features, training examples, and concepts contributed to a model's prediction. It supports models across multiple modalities such as vision and text, and can be used with little modification to the original neural network. Researchers can implement new algorithms and compare them with existing ones, and it also offers adversarial attacks and minimal input perturbation for counterfactual explanations.

It constrains generation with regular expressions and context-free grammars (CFG), and lets you naturally mix control such as conditionals, loops, and tool use with generation. Waterfall, force plots, and others visualize how much each feature pushed a prediction up or down.

L2MAC은 LLM 기반 멀티 에이전트 시스템으로 구현한 범용 저장 프로: L2MAC is a framework for a general-purpose stored-program "automatic computer" implemented as an LLM-based multi-agent system. From a one-line input prompt, it generates large outputs such as an entire complex codebase. Internally, it creates and executes a prompt program made of a series of instruction steps on its own; each step is handled by a new LLM agent, and a control unit manages the context. Agents read and write persistent memory in the form of a file store, and can use tools that run syntax checks and unit tests. The related paper was accepted at ICLR 2024.

OpenFang is an open-source agent operating system built from scratch in Rust. Instead of waiting for user input, it runs autonomous agents around the clock on a schedule to build knowledge graphs, monitor targets, find potential customers, and report results to a dashboard. It packs 7 autonomous capability packages (Hands), 30 agents, 40 channels, 38 tools, 26 LLM providers, and 16 security systems into a single binary of about 32MB. It notes that it is still pre-1.0, so compatibility may break between minor versions.

OpenAI Agents SDK는 적은 추상화로 에이전트형 AI 앱을 만: The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight package for building agentic AI apps with few abstractions, and is a production-ready upgrade of the earlier experimental project Swarm. It is built from a small set of primitives: agents equipped with instructions and tools, handoffs that pass work to other agents, and guardrails that validate inputs and outputs. Built-in tracing lets you visualize, debug, and evaluate agent flows. It supports the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs as well as more than 100 other LLMs.

Langroid는 에이전트를 일급 요소로, 멀티 에이전트 프로그래밍을 핵: Langroid is a Python LLM app framework that treats agents as first-class elements and makes multi-agent programming its core design principle. You attach an LLM, a vector store, and tools to an agent and assign it a Task, and agents collaborate by exchanging messages to solve problems. Inspired by the actor framework, it coordinates multi-agent interaction through hierarchical, recursive task delegation. It works with virtually any LLM without using LangChain or other LLM frameworks, and can also use MCP server tools.

Pydantic AI는 Python AI SDK로, 타입이 보장되고 확장: Pydantic AI is a Python AI SDK that provides a type-safe, extensible agent loop, and models can be swapped by changing just a string. The same agent can run behind a web frontend, in a terminal, on a voice call, in a durable background queue, in GitHub Actions, and more. Image generation and embeddings are included, while Pydantic Graph (typed control flow) and Pydantic Evals (testing agent behavior) are separate packages. Pydantic AI Harness adds features for long-running tasks such as memory, guardrails, subagents, planning, context management, and persistence.

It runs inside your own process with no hosted control plane, and bundles the features you need as a hand-written agent loop grows (lifecycle control such as turn limits, token budgets, and cancellation; tools; structured output; MCP; multi-agent; memory and sessions; streaming; guardrails; tracing; evaluation) into one SDK. It also provides a complete harness with optimized defaults, an agent sandbox (Box), a safe virtual shell, and an evaluation tool (evals).

Agent2Agent(A2A) 프로토콜은 서로 다른 회사가 서로 다른 프: The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol is an open protocol that aims to let generative AI agents, built by different companies with different frameworks and running on separate servers, communicate and collaborate effectively as agents rather than as tools. It aims to provide a common language for agents. With A2A, agents can discover each other's capabilities, negotiate how they interact (text, forms, media), and collaborate securely on long-running tasks. They operate without exposing their internal state, memory, or tools. The repository carries an Apache 2.0 license badge and a PyPI a2a-sdk package badge.

MCP(Model Context Protocol)는 AI 애플리케이션을: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems. It lets AI applications such as Claude or ChatGPT connect to data sources (local files, databases), tools (search engines, calculators), and workflows (specialized prompts) to access information and perform tasks. The official documentation compares it to a USB-C port for AI applications. You can build servers, clients, and MCP apps, and the project also runs an official MCP Registry (preview), which collects metadata of public MCP servers, along with a REST API. The specification repository is MIT licensed.

AGENTS.md는 '에이전트를 위한 README'로, AI 코딩 에이전: AGENTS.md is a "README for agents": a Markdown file in a set location that holds the context and instructions an AI coding agent needs to work on a project. It is separate from the human-facing README and holds agent-specific details such as build steps, tests, and coding rules. It is written in standard Markdown with no required fields, and in large monorepos you can place nested files in each subproject, with the closest file taking precedence. It is compatible with many coding agents including Codex, Jules, Cursor, Aider, and Gemini CLI, and is currently managed by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation.

AP2(Agent Payments Protocol)는 AI 에이전트가 사: AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) is an open protocol that addresses authorization, authenticity, and accountability when AI agents transact on behalf of users, and it can be used as an extension of A2A and MCP. Using Mandates (Intent Mandate and Cart Mandate), cryptographically signed digital contracts that verifiably prove user instructions, it creates a non-repudiable audit trail from intent to cart to payment. It covers both real-time purchases with a human present and delegated tasks with no human present, and it is payment-method agnostic, from credit and debit cards to stablecoins and real-time bank transfers. Google said it is working with more than 60 organizations including Adyen, American Express, Mastercard, and PayPal.

DSPy는 AI 시스템을 만드는 Python 프레임워크로, 작업을 프롬프: DSPy is a Python framework for building AI systems. It expresses a task as a structured signature (typed inputs and outputs) rather than a prompt, producing programs that are easier to maintain, modularize, and optimize. Modules let the same signature run with different strategies, such as direct prediction, step-by-step reasoning (ChainOfThought), or a tool-and-reasoning loop (ReAct). Optimizers take examples and a scoring function and automatically adjust prompts until quality converges, and they provide algorithms for optimizing prompts and weights. It can be used for anything from simple classifiers to RAG pipelines and agent loops, and it is installed with pip under the MIT license.

LlamaIndex는 문서 파싱·추출을 위한 모델을 만드는 응용 AI 연: LlamaIndex is an applied AI lab that builds models for document parsing and extraction. Its main commercial platform, LlamaParse, parses (Parse) more than 50 types of unstructured files, performs schema-based structured extraction (Extract), and offers splitting (Split), classification (Classify), and indexing (Index). It also turns handwriting, tables, and charts into structured data and catches errors with an automatic correction loop. Its open-source offerings are the LlamaIndex framework for building RAG and agent apps (300+ integration packages) and LiteParse, which parses documents locally without the cloud or LLM tokens. According to the GitHub notice, the company's main focus has shifted from the open-source framework to LlamaParse.

It encodes each passage into a token-level embedding matrix, and at search time it also embeds the query as a matrix, then finds contextually matching passages using a scalable vector-similarity operator (MaxSim). It is described as delivering higher quality than single-vector representation models while scaling efficiently to large corpora. It uses Python 3.7+, PyTorch 1.9+, and Hugging Face Transformers, can be installed with pip, and requires a GPU for training and indexing.

Med-PaLM is an LLM designed to give high-quality answers to medical questions. Its second version, Med-PaLM 2, is one of the research models that power MedLM, a family of foundation models for the healthcare industry, which Google Cloud customers can use. In the research stage, it scored 86.5% accuracy on the MedQA medical exam benchmark, and it is described as the first to reach expert level on US Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)-style questions. Research is also under way on Med-PaLM M, a multimodal version that handles images such as chest X-rays. It is noted that evaluation is still ongoing for safe and responsible use.

You upload files or connect data sources, ask questions in natural language, and get results as charts and insights. You can also create presentations, websites, reports, dashboards, images, and videos within one conversation. It supports connections to data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL, as well as Google Drive, OneDrive, and Sharepoint.

It brings model providers, coding tools, memory, skills, and scheduled tasks together in one runtime that the user controls. Sub-agents share the same execution stack, and work can be sent to other computers through named execution nodes. It also includes LemonSim, a simulation for observing and evaluating agent behavior. It is still a pre-1.0 version.

Hermes Agent는 Nous Research가 만든 자기 개선형 A: Hermes Agent is a self-improving AI agent made by Nous Research. It creates skills from experience, improves them as it is used, and comes to understand the user across sessions. You can talk to a single agent with a single memory from many places, including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, email, and CLI. It supports natural-language scheduled automation, isolated sub-agents, web search, and browser automation. It can run anywhere, from a $5 VPS to a GPU cluster or serverless infrastructure, and you can choose the model provider you want. It is free open source under the MIT license; model and hosting costs are separate.

It also has a /chat API in which every endpoint requires Bearer token authentication.

It provides a real-world economic test in which the agent earns income by completing professional job tasks from the GDPVal dataset, and must pay its own token costs and stay solvent. It measures work quality, cost efficiency, and long-term survival, and supports a competitive arena where multiple models such as GLM, Kimi, and Qwen compete against each other. It has a safety risk taxonomy, and it classifies LLM prompts (prompt classification) as well as the LLM responses to those prompts (response classification). It is a Llama2-7b model instruction-tuned on a collected dataset, and the paper states that it matched or outperformed existing content moderation tools on benchmarks such as OpenAI Moderation Evaluation and ToxicChat. It produces multi-class classification and binary decision scores, and the classification categories can be adapted to the use case, or other taxonomies can be used via zero-shot or few-shot prompting. It makes computationally intensive techniques such as optimal control, state estimation, system identification, and automatic mechanism design applicable to complex systems with many contacts. It provides a C API, Python bindings, and a Unity plugin, and supports 3D visualization with an OpenGL-based GUI.
